title: Bollinger Bands
goal: Learn how the bands grow and shrink with price swings.

objectives.text: Know that wide bands mean big swings.
Tell if price is near the top or bottom band.
Know a band touch is no signal.

slides.text: Bollinger Bands are three lines around the price. The mid line is a 20 candle average. One line is up high and one is down low.
slides.title: Three lines

slides.text: A standard deviation is a number for how much the price swings. The outer lines are 2 of these from the mid line.
slides.title: How far away

slides.text: When prices swing a lot, the bands open wide. When prices are calm, the bands get tight.
slides.title: Wide and tight

demo.caption: Real Apple prices. The bands were tight, then wide.

slides.text: Price near the top band is high for now. Price near the bottom band is low for now.
slides.title: What it tries to tell you

slides.text: Price can ride along a band for a long time. Touching a band is not a sign to buy or sell. Do not trust it alone.
slides.title: Not a signal

questions.prompt: How many lines do Bollinger Bands have?
questions.explanation: There is a mid line, plus one up and one down.
The mid line is a 20 candle average.

questions.prompt: The bands open wide. What does that mean?
questions.explanation: Wide bands mean big swings. Tight bands mean calm prices.

questions.prompt: Tight bands mean the price is calm.
questions.explanation: Yes. When swings are small, the bands squeeze in.

questions.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.

pairs.definition: A number for how much price swings

questions.explanation: The bands are built from an average and a standard deviation.

questions.prompt: Price at the top band means it must fall.
questions.explanation: No. Price can ride along a band for a long time.

questions.prompt: Price is near the bottom band. What can you say?
questions.explanation: It tells you where the price is now. It is not a promise.

questions.prompt: Turn on Bollinger Bands. Keep the rest off.
questions.explanation: Three lines show up on the chart.
